notes: Original full primary paper obtained as HTML transcription; title/authors/DOI verified. Its OCR uses p for equals, ! for less than, and 1 for greater than; quoted OCR is retained verbatim. Replication is the author-hosted full published PDF. Original study 2 and replication section 7.1 are independently matched. Replication analytic N is the sum of printed condition ns, not the overall 1018 sample. No p value inferred from an F bound. Main effect is under-specified: the original gives the same F bound for both factors, which is retained. Replication reports expertise F(1,506)=1.35, p=.247, partial eta-squared=0.00 and certainty F(1,506)=4.27, p=.039, partial eta-squared=0.01 (p. 7). No one replication test can be uniquely selected, so es and p remain null; this is locator ambiguity, not paper unavailability.
